recommendations: Your primary contest is {domesticRegionalName}. Teams studying in a host country qualify through the domestic preliminary contests.
Under Rule A6, you cannot compete in two foreign regionals. If you want to participate in a second regional, you can choose at most one foreign regional from the remaining contests.
A team can participate in at most two regionals in total (Rule A1), and must use the same team name and same three members in both.

importantRules.summary: Teams from a hosting country must qualify for their domestic regional through its corresponding preliminary contests.
Teams from a country hosting a regional should not compete in two regionals in other countries.
A team can participate in at most 2 regionals with the same team name and identical 3 contestants.

recommendations: Since your university is in {countryName} (which does not host a regional contest), your team is eligible to apply for up to any two of the {year} Asia Pacific regional contests as a foreign team.
Foreign team slots are subject to each regional site's quota and foreign selection criteria (Rule A4). Be sure to apply early on the respective contest websites.

Under Rule D4(3), your country is eligible for the Championship Wild-Card spot! The top-ranked team from each Asia Pacific country solving at least one problem qualifies directly for the Asia Pacific Championship.

importantRules.summary: A team may participate in up to 2 regionals using the same team name and identical 3 team members.
Regionals accept foreign teams from other Asia Pacific countries up to an upper bound set by each regional director.
At least one team from every Asia Pacific country (solving ≥1 problem) is guaranteed qualification to the Asia Pacific Championship.

recommendations: Teams from South Pacific (Australia, New Zealand, etc.) select their World Finals qualifiers through the South Pacific Independent Regional Contest (SPIRC), independently of Asia Pacific regionals.
Under Rule D2, the two top teams of the South Pacific Independent Regional Contest (SPIRC) are invited to compete in the Asia Pacific Championship.

Under Rule A5, your team may participate in Asia Pacific regionals as a guest team if accepted by the site director, but South Pacific teams cannot qualify for the World Finals through Asia Pacific regionals.

importantRules.summary: South Pacific teams qualify for the World Finals through the South Pacific Independent Regional Contest, not APAC regionals.
The two top teams of the South Pacific Independent Regional Contest are invited to compete in the Asia Pacific Championship.

recommendations: Your university is located outside the Asia Pacific and South Pacific super-regions (e.g. Asia East, Asia West, Europe, Americas).
World Finals qualification for your university must be earned through your home super-region's designated regional contests.

Under Rule A5, Asia Pacific regionals may accept teams from other super-regions as guest teams at the director's discretion, but these teams cannot qualify for the World Finals through Asia Pacific regionals.

importantRules.summary: Regionals may accept teams from other super-regions as guest teams, but they are never qualified for the World Finals through Asia Pacific regionals.
